statement: For Bernoulli nearest-neighbor bond percolation on Z^d, d>=1, at any p in [0,1], theta_d(p)=lim_{n->infinity} P_p(0 is connected to the vertex boundary of [-n,n]^d).
assumptions: Independent Bernoulli(p) nearest-neighbor edges
Vertex boundary in the infinity norm
The parameter p is fixed before taking n to infinity
proof: The events A_n are decreasing: a nearest-neighbor path to the boundary of a larger box must meet the smaller boundary. Their intersection is the event that the origin cluster is unbounded. A bounded subset of Z^d is finite, so unboundedness is equivalent to infinitude. Continuity from above of a probability measure gives the formula.

statement: For a strongly R-dependent binary field on Z^2, R>=0 integer, with each bad-site probability at most q in [0,1], the probability that m distinct given sites are all bad is at most q^ceil(m/(R+1)^2).
assumptions: Independence of sigma-fields on index sets whose infinity-norm separation exceeds R
proof: Color by both residues modulo R+1. The largest color subfamily has at least ceil(m/(R+1)^2) sites and is jointly independent. The all-bad event implies all sites of that subfamily are bad.

Uniform bad-site probability bound q in [0,1]
Nearest-neighbor good connectivity and star-neighbor bad circuits
